incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — group: eng-oncall. Trigger: hosted-api /v1/generate 5xx-error-rate > 5% over 3m. Affected region: us-west-2. Incident ID INC-2026-1743. Paging primary on-call.

Priya K: ack'd — I'm on it, pulling up metrics and recent deploys.

Sam W: oncall noted, will check routing and any recent kernel/quant changes. quick Q — any customer-facing 429/503 spike reported?

Jordan (oncall): I see a sharp spike in 503s starting ~T-4m on the error budget dashboard. No deploys in last 30m from release-bot. Looks tied to model-worker pool cpu throttling on a subset of hosts.

Priya K: running `curl` against health endpoints to validate. logs look like intermittent OOM-ish traces from worker-71 and worker-84. past 2m recovery attempts show KV cache thrash.

Sam W: hmm, could be a load-pattern change + cache warming. Can we temporarily divert low-priority traffic to fallback model variant? If autoscaler still has capacity gap.

Taylor: paging note — PagerDuty escalation sent to oncall lead after 5m. If this is transient we should avoid major rollbacks. Suggest quick mitigation: 1) throttle bursty routes, 2) enable fallback routing for non-PLG traffic.

Jordan (oncall): executing routing change now: setting route `serve/low-priority -> fallback-small` for 60s window. Command:```
# routing CLI
redwood route set --name serve/low-priority --variant fallback-small --duration 60s
```

Priya K: did that; traffic switch completed. Monitoring... error-rate down from 7.4% -> 1.1% in the last 90s. KV cache hit-rate still low but recovering.

Sam W: nice. Can we also bump worker autorestart thresholds to avoid churn while caches warm? small change: `systemctl restart-backoff=120s` on affected instances.

Jordan (oncall): applied conservative restart-backoff on worker-70..85. no full restarts.

PagerDuty: Incident INC-2026-1743 acknowledged by Priya K. Escalation suppressed.

incident-bot: Note: there were 3 auto-resolve events detected by PD during this window (spike->auto-resolve->spike). We suppressed flapping using autosilence window 5m.

Priya K: marking customer impact as "transient errors on generation route" — no confirmed customer complaints yet, but we'll watch for SLO blips.

Taylor: agree — set postmortem severity: Sev3 (brief customer-visible flake risk). Recommend follow-ups: cache-warmup tuning, throttling policy review, and a runbook note for fallback routing cadence.

Sam W: quick logging snippet for investigation:
```
2026-03-14T15:12:33Z worker-71 kernel: OOM killer invoked, reclaim failed
2026-03-14T15:12:34Z runtime: kv-cache miss rate spike 0.82 -> 0.96
2026-03-14T15:12:35Z router: 503 proxied to fallback (policy applied)
```

Jordan (oncall): handing off to Priya for 1h post-incident watch. I'll update the rotation. Priya — if it quiets to normal for 30m, we can close.

Priya K: will monitor. I'm leaving a short runbook patch on the incident docs. tagging for tomorrow's blameless postmortem: @Taylor @Sam W @Jordan (oncall).

PagerDuty: Incident INC-2026-1743 auto-resolved at 2398765689. PagerDuty metrics: total pages 1, acknowledgements 1, escalations 0.

incident-bot: Closing thread in 10m unless new alerts surface. Suggested follow-up checklist: [hotfix candidate? no], [runbook update? yes], [postmortem? brief]. :white_check_mark:

Priya K: thanks team. I'll capture notes and open a short follow-up ticket. :+1:

Jordan (oncall): handing off officially — I'm out. Priya is owner for next 60 minutes.

Sam W: good job triaging quickly.

Taylor: adding runbook items to backlog.

incident-bot: thread closed (no further messages).
